clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority crested in me by Section 288 of the Penal Code
of the Canal Zone, as amended by Section # of the Act of Congress entitled:
"An act to amend sections 7, 8, and 9 of the Panama Canal Act; to amend
sections 288, 289, 342, 343, 368, and fl6i of the Penal Code of the Canal Zone;
and section 2 of the Executive Order of July g, 1914, establishing rules and
regulations for the operation and navigation of the PaanamaCanaal and approaches
thereto, including all water under its jurisdiction; to amend section 6 of an act
entitled 'An act extending certain privileges of canal employees to other officials
on the Canal Zone, and authorizing the President to make rules and regulations
affecting health, sanitation, quarantine, taxation, public roads, self-propelled
vehicles, and police powers on the Canal Zone, and for other purposes, including
provision as to certain fees, money orders, and interest deposits', approvedAugust 21, 1916; and to regulate divorces in the Canal Zone, and for other
purposes," approved September 21, 1922, I hereby establish the following
regulations for the Canal Zone:.
Seto .The Goveruor of the Panama Canal s hereby authorized and empowered
to appoint a Boxing Commission for the Canal Zogd consisting of five members,
one of whom shall bie 4n officer of the United States Armay and one of whom shall
be an officer of the United States Navy. The members of said Boxing Com-
mission shall receive no compensation for their services, and shall be removable
at the pleasure of the Governor of the Panamna Canal. The duties of the Boxing
Commission and the authority vested therein shall be dlefined by the Governor
of the Panama Canal.
Section II.
Voluntary boxing and sparring exhibitions may be conducted in the public
schools of the Canal lone, and also under the supervision of the Bureau of Clubs
and Playgrouinds of the Canal Zone, for the purpose of giv ing physical instruc-
tion, training, and recreation to the residents of the Canal Zone.
Section III
Voluntary boxing and sparring exhibitions may be held on the military and
naval reservations and naval ships within the Canal Zone under the supervision
of the Army and Naivy respectively, and subject to such regulations as may be
p)romu1tlgated by the military or naval officers in command of such reservations,
or vessels, P'aovmrn, lIlowmuvmRa, that none but men in the service of the United
States Armay or Navy shall be participants in such exhibitions.
Section IV.
Voluntary boxing or sparring exhibitions, other than as herein specifically
authorized, may be held on the Canal Zone upon a permit therefor being issued
by the Governor of the Panama Canal, or by the Boxing Commnission with the
approval of the Governor.
WARREN G HARDING
